status: SOURCED 8 Oct 2026, ready to build to. Book values from Ellis 1902 pp.90-93 and 111-112, gaps filled from Hasluck 1907 pp.346-347 and 398 and Riley 1905 pp.353-357 (each labelled). The photograph P1 (Teignmouth, four-panel, frontal) decides every point where it disagrees with a book (Jafar's ruling). Every value has its row in SOURCES.md section 1 with Read / Scaled / Derived / Photo / Judgement. self_check below is written by self_check.py.
axes: x across the opening (left to right seen from outside), z up, y depth into the wall with the outside at -y. Origin: the left brick reveal edge (x=0), the top of the stone sill under the leaf (z=0), the outside face of the brick wall (y=0).

opening._src: Derived: clear between stops (772.0) plus the jamb showing past the brick each side (55, Photo P1). Height: sill top to brick head = leaf gap 10 + leaf 1948 - stop 22 + 1.6 + transom face 65 + glass sight 267 + head showing 60. See SOURCES.md 1a, 1f.
opening._reveal: Read: '18-in. brick wall with 4 1/2-in. reveals', Hasluck p.346 (outer four-panel door with fanlight). Same figure as Ellis's sash frame set-back (lab 2 SOURCES 1b).
opening._wall: Judgement: 1 1/2 brick (13 1/2 in), the wall Ellis draws for the sash (lab 2 SOURCES 1a); Hasluck's example is 18 in. Only the reveal matters to this target.

game_present.fanlight: none (brick spandrel 869 high above the leaf)
game_present._src: ledger repo origin/wip production/specs/vignette-pieces.json, C9_door_side rows (e.g. east_parade_sidedoor0)

leaf._w: Read: 2 ft 8 in between the frame's rebates, Hasluck p.347 Fig. 1148 (the dimension's witness lines touch the rebate faces, checked by zoom)
leaf._h: Photo: P1's visible leaf (stop to stop, sill to transom) is 2.505 +-0.04 times as high as wide; with the width above and the stops' 22 mm cover this gives 1948 +-31. Hasluck's printed 6 ft 8 in (2032) would show 2.63: outside the photo's error, so the photo wins (SOURCES.md 3, D1).
leaf._t: Read: entrance doors '2 to 2 1/2 in. thick', Ellis p.93; '2-in. four-panel door', Hasluck p.398. Hasluck Fig. 1148 scales 53.
leaf._pos: Derived: left rebate face at x=33.0 plus 1.6 clearance; leaf bottom 10 above the stone sill (Photo P1, gap 2 px +-1 px = 10 +-5)
leaf._y: Derived: reveal 114.3 + stop depth 74.0 (frame 127 less rebate 53)
leaf._clear: Judgement: 1/16 in, the sash play Hasluck gives on p.404 (no door figure found)
leaf._stile: Read: 'stiles and top rails ... out of 4 1/2 in.', Ellis p.93; Riley p.357 Fig. 671 prints 4 1/2 for an outer door. Photo P1 agrees (115.4 +-11).
leaf._muntin: Photo: P1 shows 23.8 px = 122.6 +-15 between the panel mouldings; the outside bolection mouldings cover 4.8 of each edge, so the muntin is 132.2. Ellis p.93 and Riley p.357 both print 4 in (101.6), outside the error: the photo wins (D2). P2 (six-panel) shows about 107.
leaf._top: Read: Riley p.357 Fig. 670 prints 5 in for an outer door's top rail, and P1 agrees (20.3 px showing = 104.5, plus 22 behind the transom stop and 4.8 under the moulding = 131.3 +-12). Ellis p.93's 4 1/2 in (114.3) is outside the photo's error (D8).
leaf._lock: Read: 'middle and bottom rails 9 in.', Ellis p.93. P1 agrees: 210 +-15 showing between the mouldings plus two 4.8 laps = 219.6. Riley's outer door prints 11 in (279), outside the error, not used.
leaf._lockc: Photo: P1, 153 px x 5.15 = 787 +-12. Ellis p.93 says 2 ft 8 in, 'about 6 in. lower' when approached from a step (660); Riley p.355 says about 2 ft 9 in (838). Photo wins (D3).
leaf._bottom: Photo: P1, 36.5 px = 188 +-15 from the leaf bottom to the moulding edge, plus a 4.8 lap. Ellis 9 in (228.6) and Riley 11 in are outside the error; photo wins (D4).
leaf.construction: Read: stiles run full height; rails tenoned through the stiles; muntins stub-tenoned into the rails (Ellis p.90 Fig. 290; Riley p.353 Fig. 654 'stump tenon').

panels._layout: Four panels, two tall above the lock rail and two short below (Ellis Fig. 290; Riley Fig. 654; Photo P1). Positions are in leaf coordinates: u from the leaf's left edge, v from its bottom. Each is the framing opening (edge of stile, rail, muntin).
panels._openings: Derived from the leaf numbers above (panel openings 226.0 wide; top 919.7 high, bottom 479.9 high)
panels._groove: Read: 'usually grooved 1/2 in. deep for the panels', Ellis p.92 (5/8 in over 2 ft wide; these are 241 wide)
panels._play: Read: panels 'given 1/8 in. play sideways, but fitting close lengthways of the grain', Ellis p.92. Taken as 1/8 in in total across the width (Judgement on the reading).
panels._thick: Derived: panels 'usually about one-third the thickness of the door', Riley p.353; 50.8 / 3. Riley p.355 notes outer doors' lower panels are often two-thirds and bead flush; P1 shows moulded lower panels, so one-third is kept.
panels.position_in_thickness: centred (Read: panels 'fit into grooves in the middle of the framing', Riley p.353)
panels.type_outside: flat panel with a bolection moulding (Read: 'Bolection mould' on the outside of the four-panelled outer door, Riley p.357 Fig. 671; P1 shows a raised moulding round a flat field, consistent)
panels.type_inside: flat panel, single (planted, sunk) moulding (Read: 'Single mould', Riley p.357 Fig. 671)

outside_bolection.kind: bolection, planted, fixed to the panel, rebated over the framing
outside_bolection._w: Scaled: Riley p.357 Fig. 671 against its printed 4 1/2 in stile, +-5. Photo P1: 38 +-10 (agrees).
outside_bolection._lap: Read: 'From 1/8 to 3/16 in. is sufficient', Ellis p.92 (bolection lap). 3/16 in used.
outside_bolection.profile: ogee and fillet, rebated over the framing edge (Ellis p.91 Fig. 294-295, drawn; no numbers)

inside_single.kind: planted sunk moulding, fixed to the framing, flush with its face
inside_single.profile: ogee/ovolo; back edge bevelled under (Read: Ellis p.91 'The back edge of the moulding should be bevelled under')

lock_rail_band.kind: projecting horizontal moulding across the full width of the lock rail
lock_rail_band._src: Photo: P1, rows 363-379 px. Not in any book read. Projection Judgement (the band throws a 3 px shadow).

weatherboard.kind: weather moulding across the bottom rail, outside
weatherboard._src: Photo: P1, rows 515-529 px. Not in any book read. Projection Judgement.

mouldings._ovolo: Read: 'the outside edge of the frame has an ovolo worked on', Hasluck p.346; 'Ovolo mould', Riley p.357. Size Scaled from Hasluck Fig. 1148, +-5.

frame.kind: solid frame, rebated out of the solid; jambs framed between head and sill (Read: Ellis p.111)
frame._jamb: Read: '5 x 4 rebated frame', Riley p.357 Fig. 671; Scaled: Hasluck Fig. 1148 frame 103 across by 126 deep, so 4 in across the opening and 5 in into the wall
frame._showing: Photo: P1, left 10 px and right 11 px x 5.15 = 52 and 57, +-10. Hasluck Fig. 1148 scales 39 (photo wins, D5).
frame._rebate_w: Scaled: the stop covers the leaf by 20 (Hasluck Fig. 1148) and 24 (Riley Fig. 671), mean 22 +-5
frame._rebate_d: Scaled: Hasluck Fig. 1148 (leaf 2 in plus play)
frame._stop: Derived: 127 - 53; the stop is on the outside, the leaf opens inwards (Hasluck Figs. 1148-1149, Riley Fig. 671)
frame._head: Section Read as the jambs (Riley 'Transome 5 x 4' and frame 5 x 4). Showing 60 is Photo P1 (11.5 px). Ellis p.111: the head is built into the wall under the arch or fixed to a lintel.
frame._transom: Photo: P1 shows 12.5 px = 65 +-10 between the leaf and the glass. Riley prints a 5 x 4 transom (101.6 high); photo wins (D6). Hasluck p.398: 'double rebated and weathered transom'.

sill.kind: stone sill, no oak sill; frame feet held by iron plugs

frame._sill: Read: 'The foot of the frame, when an oak sill is not framed in, is secured to the stone sill by iron plugs', Ellis p.111. Thickness Photo P1 (14 px = 72 +-10, rounded to 3 in, Judgement). Front flush with the wall face and nosing rounded: Photo P1. Back edge: Judgement, under the frame's inside face.

fanlight.kind: fixed single pane glazed straight into the frame, no sash, no bars

frame._fanlight: Photo: P1 glass 51.5 px = 267 +-10 high, as wide as the leaf's visible width. Hasluck p.347 prints a 1 ft 6 in (457) hung fanlight; photo wins (D7). Glass 21 oz sheet 2.5 (Rivington Part III p.440, lab 2 SOURCES 1e). Rebate 1/4 in: Judgement from Ellis's sash rebate p.127. Glass plane 19 behind the frame face: Judgement.

brick.head_kind: flat or slightly cambered brick arch over the frame head (Photo P1; Ellis p.111 Fig. 355 shows a segmental arch on the head)
